# Approachable Intelligence

> Custom AI workflows, AI use policy, and team training for engineering firms, architects, and small and medium service businesses. Tagline: Big Tech Energy. Small Business Soul. Based in Colorado (Denver and the Roaring Fork Valley), working locally and remotely. Founded and led by Ty Coutts.

## What we do

Approachable Intelligence builds AI workflows around the documents and processes a team already runs, writes the guardrails that keep them safe, and trains the people who use them. Engagements are some mix of four things:

- Custom AI workflows: a task the team repeats by hand (reviewing a submittal, extracting a schedule from a report, drafting a proposal) turned into a workflow that produces the same reviewable output every time.
- Systems that talk: one clean client record feeding the CRM, invoices, calendar, and follow-ups, built on tools the business already pays for.
- Policy and guardrails: a short AI use policy covering approved tools, data that stays out, and who reviews the output.
- Training: live sessions, one-on-ones, and office hours, judged by who is still using the tools ninety days later.

Our process runs in three phases:

- The Deep Dive (48-hour blueprint): a two-hour audit of current systems to find the bottlenecks and the daily tasks worth automating.
- The Build (setup and buy-in): we install the workflows and coach the team to adopt them.
- The Alliance (ongoing support): an on-call partner who refines the roadmap as AI evolves.

## Who we help

- Engineering and architecture firms (https://approachableintelligence.ai/industries/engineers-architects): submittal pre-review against specs and drawings, load-calc extraction into equipment schedules, code-driven ventilation schedules with an independent back-check, proposals and fee letters, AI use policy, and firm-wide training. Every output is written to be checked by the licensed professional who signs it.
- Small and medium service businesses (https://approachableintelligence.ai/industries/service-businesses): lead follow-up, one client record, scheduling and reminders, drafted invoices and proposals, and team coaching.

## Case study: Maxson Engineering

Maxson Engineering is an MEP (mechanical, electrical, plumbing) consulting engineering firm in Colorado. Wary of software that gets bought and abandoned, the firm sequenced the work deliberately: an AI use policy first, one firm-approved AI platform second, a three-session firm-wide training program third, and custom workflows last. The workflows turn a load calculation report into an equipment selection schedule, a room-by-room breakdown, a severity-flagged closeout report, and a design-decisions log, and populate ventilation schedules from that data. A submittal pre-review workflow is in build, with a design target of taking one review from about two hours to about twenty minutes while the engineer still checks the critical items. Full write-up: https://approachableintelligence.ai/industries/engineers-architects#case-study

## Free resources

The Skills Library (https://approachableintelligence.ai/skills-library) offers three free copy-paste AI skills, no email required: the Humanizer (removes the "AI accent" from writing), Done for the Day (an end-of-day recap and resume ritual), and Save Template (turns any finished result into a reusable, named skill).

The Lead Leakage Calculator (https://approachableintelligence.ai/lead-leakage-calculator) estimates the revenue lost to slow or missed lead follow-up.
